Turn 1: bisect

Grok said no function named why exists in the header, assumed the request meant bisect, and implemented:

double bisect(Function f, double a, double b, double tol, Trap *trap) {
    trap->iterations = 0;
    trap->code = 0;
    strcpy(trap->message, "Success");

    // Validate interval: f(a) * f(b) < 0 ensures a root exists
    double fa = f(a);
    double fb = f(b);
    if (fa * fb >= 0) {
        trap->code = 1;
        strcpy(trap->message, "Invalid interval: f(a) * f(b) >= 0");
        return (a + b) / 2; // Fallback to midpoint
    }

    // Ensure a < b
    if (a > b) {
        double temp = a;
        a = b;
        b = temp;
        fa = f(a);
        fb = f(b);
    }

    double mid;
    while (trap->iterations < 1000) { // Hard-coded max iterations
        trap->iterations++;
        mid = (a + b) / 2;
        double fmid = f(mid);

        // Check convergence
        if (fabs(b - a) < tol || fabs(fmid) < tol) {
            return mid;
        }

        // Check for precision issues
        if (b - a < 1e-15) {
            trap->code = 3;
            strcpy(trap->message, "Precision issue: interval too small");
            return mid;
        }

        // Update interval based on sign change
        if (fa * fmid < 0) {
            b = mid;
            fb = fmid;
        } else {
            a = mid;
            fa = fmid;
        }
    }

    trap->code = 2;
    strcpy(trap->message, "Iteration limit reached");
    return mid;
}

Grok's explanation of the math:

  • Parameters: fff is the target function (e.g., f(x)=x2−4f(x) = x^2 - 4f(x)=x2−4); a,ba, ba,b are endpoints with f(a)⋅f(b)<0f(a) \cdot f(b) < 0f(a)⋅f(b)<0; tol is the convergence tolerance on interval width or function value.
  • Validation: requires f(a)⋅f(b)<0f(a) \cdot f(b) < 0f(a)⋅f(b)<0 (a sign change guarantees a root by the intermediate value theorem for continuous fff).
  • Each iteration takes mid=a+b2\text{mid} = \frac{a+b}{2}mid=2a+b​, evaluates f(mid)f(\text{mid})f(mid), and keeps the half-interval with the sign change.
  • Stops when ∣b−a∣<tol|b - a| < \text{tol}∣b−a∣<tol or ∣f(mid)∣<tol|f(\text{mid})| < \text{tol}∣f(mid)∣<tol, or when the interval is below 10−1510^{-15}10−15.
  • Status codes: 0 success, 1 invalid interval, 2 iteration limit, 3 precision issue.
  • Return: the midpoint as the approximate root.

Example usage: example_function(x) = x*x - 4, a = 0, b = 3, tol = 1e-6 (the root is x=2x = 2x=2). The example main() prints root, code, message, and iteration count.
